text:
maya: quick ask — can someone run a short latency run comparing hosted vs onprem after the kernel bump? p95 on onprem jumped in the last deploy.

maya: ```./infra/bench/latency_runner --model redwood/small --seq 1024 --concurrency 4 --warmup 200 --iters 2000 --report p50,p95```

aj: I can run on onprem-01 tonight. which vpc node do you want to compare? vpc-west-2-03 ok?

maya: vpc-west-2-03 is fine. please use the same env (`PYTHONPATH`, same wheel). also capture perf/flamegraph: `perf record -F 99 -g -- ./serve_bench && perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded && flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg`

samira: also pls note gro/lro settings — last time GRO masked a noisy IRQ path. if possible capture `ethtool -k` output.

juan: fyi kernel bumped from 5.15.0-89 -> 5.15.0-92 on the onprem hosts last night.

aj: starting now on onprem-01. infra-bot: Bench job started: https://ci.redwood/bench/2090012345 (job id 6721)

infra-bot: job 6721 logs streaming -> https://ci.redwood/bench/logs/6721

aj: quick note — saw a TCP retransmit spike during warmup on onprem-01, capturing pcap + perf.

maya: can you drop the pcap and perf data in `/tmp/bench-2090012345/` on the jump host?

aj: done — `/tmp/bench-2090012345/pcap.pcap` and `/tmp/bench-2090012345/perf.data` uploaded to the artifacts bucket.

samira: I can take the flamegraph tomorrow AM. tagging @juan — can you confirm NIC offload settings for the onprem hosts? `ethtool -k onprem-01` would help.

juan: on onprem-01: rx-checksumming: on, tx-checksumming: on, gro: on, lro: off. I can flip gro off on a spare host to test.

maya: let's not change config mid-run. if aj can repro with gro off on a spare host that's safer.

aj: spun up onprem-02 with gro=off and re-ran. short results: hosted p95 48ms, vpc p95 52ms, onprem-01 p95 117ms, onprem-02 (gro off) p95 62ms.

maya: that's telling — big delta on onprem-01 only. can you upload folded stacks and flamegraphs?

aj: uploaded `out.folded` and flamegraph gist -> https://gist.github.com/aj/bench-2090012345

samira: quick look at the flamegraph — lots of time in netdev rx path and a syscall wait around the NIC driver. seems like a packet-handling stall. i'm opening a tiny PR to add a perf marker and bump `net.core.netdev_max_backlog` for the bench nodes so we can see impact. PR #1284.

maya: pinging samira to review PR #1284. also we should run the same bench on a host freshly provisioned with kernel 5.15.0-92 to rule out config drift.

samira: ack, will review tonight and add notes.

juan: i can repro on a staging rack tomorrow and run both kernel-89 and kernel-92 for comparison.

maya: thanks all — i'll capture this in infra-qa/benching.md and follow up if we need a hotfix. :thumbsup:

aj: thanks — leaving pcap/perf in the bench dir and closing job 6721 (will keep job artifacts for 7 days).
